Hierarchical sampling adds overhead for coarse evaluation but reduces the number of fine samples needed for high-quality rendering [S1].

The evidence in Source [S1] explicitly describes a 'hierarchical sampling strategy' (Section 4.1). It states that this strategy first samples coarse points to obtain a density estimate, which is then used to sample fine points with importance sampling. The text notes that evaluating density with the dense grid at coarse points might skip important regions, implying the coarse evaluation is a necessary step (overhead) to guide the fine sampling. By using the coarse estimate to perform importance sampling for the fine points, the method reduces the number of fine samples needed to achieve high-quality rendering (by focusing samples on high-density areas). The claim accurately reflects the mechanism described: coarse evaluation is performed (adding some computational step/overhead compared to direct fine sampling) to reduce the number of fine samples required for quality.
